english.title: Sponsor fail to report list of suspected unexpected serious adverse reactions

additionalkeywords.additionalkeyword: Medicines for Human Use Clinical trials Regulations 2004

english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) being the sponsor of a clinical trial, failed as soon as practicable after the end of the reporting year in relation to each investigational medicinal product tested in clinical trials in the United Kingdom for which you were the sponsor, to furnish the licensing authority and the relevant ethics committees, namely **(..SPECIFY THE NAME / NAMES OF THE AUTHORITY / COMMITTEE..) with

(A)_[a list of all the suspected serious adverse reactions which occurred during that year in relation to those trials at trial sites in the United Kingdom or elsewhere]_
(B)_[a list of all the suspected serious adverse reactions which occurred during that year in relation to trials, other than clinical trials relating to that product which were conducted outside the United Kingdom for which you were the sponsor]_
(C)_[a report on the safety of the subjects of those trials]_
english.legislation: Contrary to regulations 35(1), 49(1)(j) and 52 of the Medicines for Human Use (Clinical Trials) Regulations 2004.

english.notes: (i) Regulation 51 of the of the Medicines for Human Use (Clinical Trials) Regulations 2004 provides a defence of due diligence.(iii) This offence no longer applies from the 27th April 2026 due to changes made by the Medicines for Human Use (Clinical Trials) (Amendment) Regulations 2025.
